ai.description: *Uropeltis maculata* reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown with irregular yellow spots and a distinct, truncated, shield-like tail. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis maculata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, sharp-edged, keeled terminal shield (caudal disc) that is clearly separated from the dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis maculata* inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of evergreen and shola forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Earth Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its time burrowing through loose soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis maculata* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis maculata* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
